summary: Day 85 (Saturday May 23). **AL JAZEERA MAY 22 MENTIONED 'EU MOVES TO SANCTION IRAN OVER HORMUZ BLOCKADE' — REPORTED LOW-CONFIDENCE; NOT YET INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED BY REUTERS/FT/POLITICO EUROPE/EURACTIV. If REAL, would mark BREAKDOWN OF EUROPEAN 'WE'RE NOT IN THIS FIGHT' POSITIONING THAT HAS HELD SINCE MARCH. If NOT REAL, single-source Gulf-media framing being floated to pressure Iran into deal acceptance.** Trigger to watch: official EU Council statement OR Federica Mogherini-successor statement on Iran sanctions within 7 days = confirmation; silence by May 30 = Al Jazeera framing was speculative. **TTF Gas €48.69/MWh May 22 close (-1.46% 1D, +2.1% MoM, +30%+ vs ~€31 baseline)** — flat-to-easing; Qatar Ras Laffan FM 17% liquefaction persists but Norway maintenance ease holding. **The European posture is 'watching the US-Iran-Pakistan-Gulf track resolve, not intervening'**: Reuters Europe / Politico Europe / Euractiv silent on Munir visit beyond wire amplification; no fresh emergency measures published. ECB Lagarde 'new energy shock' framing carries forward as operative anchor; ECB holds 2.15%. **The trigger 'TTF crosses €70/MWh sustained 5 sessions' remains NOT activated** (current €48.69 vs €70 threshold). PRIOR (May 16): **TTF €49.86/MWh May 15 (+4.63% 1D, third consecutive daily increase, highest since April; ~+60% from pre-war €31.20)** — driver chain ongoing Qatar Ras Laffan force majeure on ~17% of liquefaction capacity (recovery 'in years not months'); Hormuz tensions; Europe's pre-winter storage rebuild. **Europe is no longer in 'alarm nor relief' mode but in 'creeping pricing-in' mode** — the Goldman tail scenario of ~€72/MWh remains above today's print but the trajectory has clearly turned over the past week. **DAX -2.1% 1D**: HeidelbergCement -7.16%, Siemens -4.94%, MTU Aero -4.87% — capex-intensive industrials hit on inflation/yield-shock + Iran stall. **ECB Lagarde 'new energy shock: economic scenarios and policy implications' May 6 speech framing structural-energy-inflation regime** continues to be the operative anchor. ECB held 2.15% in April; next decision approaches with the inflation-pass-through case strengthening. **The trigger 'TTF crosses €70/MWh sustained 5 sessions' is NOT activated but the +4.63% acceleration that crossed €48 and €49 in one session is the cleanest pricing-in signal of the week.** PRIOR (April 28): Day 61 Tuesday. ECB APRIL 29-30 MEETING IN <48 HOURS — HOLD AT 2.15% MOST PROBABLE; MERZ 'HUMILIATING' FRAMING IS THE EUROPEAN-LEADERSHIP TONE SHIFT TO WATCH. Per Irish Times Apr 27, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz publicly stated that Iran is 'humiliating' the US as talks stall. This is the first major European G7 leader to characterize the diplomatic deadlock in such pointed terms. Operationally significant because Germany has been the European energy-vulnerability bellwether on this crisis. Merz's characterization implies (a) European patience with the US-led blockade is finite, (b) European preference for de-escalation may override Atlantic-alliance restraint as winter-2026 storage refill begins, (c) European institutional capital (ABP, Norges Bank) may find this characterization easier to act on than mainstream Atlanticist coverage. No US response yet. Macron / Starmer have not echoed. TTF €45.17/MWh Apr 27 (+0.75% 1D, +0.5% 1M; €31 pre-crisis = €14 of crisis premium). Critically below the €70 cascade-intensity threshold (industrial demand destruction; German PMI contracts hard). ECB has NOT characterized Hormuz risk as systemic. Holds 2.15%. ECB next decision April 29-30. Stagflation framing (inflation 2.6% forecast 2026, spiking to 3.1% Q2) intact. Bond reaction Friday: 10Y 4.31% (-0.3%) range-bound. recent_signals.headline: **THE ECB MEETS THURSDAY 23 JULY into a gas shock its own projections do not capture.** Markets price ~95.3% hold (3.4% for +25bp). This is a NON-PROJECTION meeting, so June's staff forecasts stand unrevised — and those put 2026 headline inflation at 3.0% with **Q3 energy inflation at 12.5%, a forecast made BEFORE TTF broke EUR57.** The ECB hiked 25bp on 11 June (deposit rate 2.25%, MRO 2.40%, MLF 2.65%, effective 17 Jun) — its first hike in three years, explicitly attributed to the energy path. CNBC's European desk reports an ECB rates rethink amid an 'extremely volatile' outlook. The physical backdrop is worse than the price: EU gas storage 53% full against a 75% five-year norm (lowest in 15 years), July injections at a six-year low, net injections since April covering only 40% of winter need, and **Brussels has already RELAXED the mandatory storage target from 90% to 80% with a further 4% deviation allowed — a regulator conceding the target is unreachable before winter begins.** Germany has passed a two-month, EUR1.6bn fuel-tax relief with petrol above the symbolic EUR2/litre — the political tell that this has stopped being a market story there. CONFIRMED.

**The ECB will HOLD Thursday 23 July, with September flagged as the 'reckoning.'** Eurozone CPI is 2.8% (20 Jul); this is a NON-projection meeting, so June's stale Q3 energy-inflation forecast (12.5%, set before TTF broke EUR57) stands unrevised while **TTF is now EUR61.37 (+44.8% 1M, a new cycle high)** on the continued absence of Qatari LNG through Hormuz. Like the Fed, the ECB is treating a genuine supply shock as deferrable — the September meeting, with fresh projections, is where the energy path bites. CONFIRMED.

**The ECB PAUSED on 23 July, explicitly citing Middle East/oil risk — the stagflation frame now has central-bank confirmation.** Reuters: 'ECB to pause rate hikes but may signal more is needed'; Anadolu: 'remains cautious amid Middle East risks'; France 24: 'New Mideast fighting puts eurozone rate-setters on alert.' Eurozone CPI 2.8%; a non-projection meeting, so June's stale Q3 energy-inflation forecast (12.5%) stands unrevised while TTF prints a fresh cycle high (EUR63.75). **September is flagged as the decision point, and the debate is a HIKE not a cut** — i.e. the ECB is deferring the energy shock to Q3 exactly as the Fed is. This confirms the 'September reckoning' the graph flagged. CONFIRMED (decision landing just after the data window; well-corroborated).
